title: Howard Lutnick, Cantor Fitzgerald and Tether
summary: The financial ties are well documented. Cantor custodies Tether's Treasury reserves and holds a $600M convertible bond convertible into ~5% of Tether, negotiated in 2024 under Lutnick. Lutnick signed all his sale agreements on 16 May 2025 (BGC and Newmark buybacks took effect that day), but the sale of his Cantor interest, to buyers the White House names as 26North, Oak Hill Advisors and Cantor Fitzgerald, L.P. (Cantor says trusts for his children), closed only on 6 Oct 2025 after regulatory approvals, per his own 278-T; in between, a limited White House waiver (8 Jul 2025) let him take part in broad policy matters affecting the firms; Bloomberg reported that Tether lent to one of those trusts under a credit document filed on 7 Oct 2025, around the same time. Cantor's SPAC took the Tether/Bitfinex/SoftBank-backed Twenty One Capital public, and Cantor is custodian for Tether's GENIUS-compliant USAT. No policy action by Lutnick or Commerce benefiting Tether is documented, and no link between Tether and chip-export licences was found.

sub_claims.finding: WSJ (Nov 2024) reported Cantor holds most of Tether's ~$133B in assets for tens of millions of dollars a year in fees. Lutnick acknowledged the custody at his 29 Jan 2025 hearing. Cantor is also USAT's reserve custodian and primary dealer (Jan 2026).

sub_claims.statement: Cantor held a stake in Tether.
sub_claims.finding: The holding is a $600M convertible bond that converts into ~5% equity. Lutnick helped negotiate it in April 2024 and testified it is not direct equity. Sen. Blumenthal estimates its value at ~$10B (unverified estimate). Context for that estimate: Tether sought to raise $15-20B at a ~$500B valuation from Sept 2025, cut the target raise to ~$5B after investor pushback (FT, Feb 2026) and set a two-week commitment deadline in April 2026; no closed round at $500B was found. A 5% stake would be ~$25B at $500B, so the ~$10B estimate implies a much lower valuation.

sub_claims.statement: Lutnick divested and Cantor is now run by his sons.
sub_claims.finding: Lutnick was confirmed 18 Feb 2025 (51-45). The divestiture package was announced 19 May 2025 and parts took effect 16 May 2025 (BGC bought back shares for $151.5M, Newmark for $127M), but the transfer of his Cantor interest to trusts for his children was to close after regulatory approvals (expected Q3 2025); Bloomberg later reported the sale to the trusts happened in October 2025; his 278-T (signed 5 Nov 2025) dates it exactly: 'entered into May 16, 2025 ... and consummated on October 6, 2025 following regulatory approvals', and lists Cantor Fitzgerald, L.P., CF Group Management, Inc., his BGC Class B shares and smaller interests. Brandon is chairman/CEO and controlling trustee, Kyle executive vice chair, and Cantor's announcement put 26North and Glenn August (founder of Oak Hill Advisors) in as minority owners; the White House waiver names the buyers as '26 North, Oak Hill Advisors and Cantor Fitzgerald, L.P.'.

sub_claims.statement: Tether financed the children's trust during the divestiture.
sub_claims.finding: Bloomberg (18 Mar 2026) reported Tether lent an undisclosed sum to 'Dynasty Trust A', under a New York credit document filed on 7 Oct 2025, secured by 'all assets' of the trust; a Cantor executive said it was backed by the Tether convertible bond. Bloomberg reported the sale of Lutnick's Cantor stake to the trusts took place in October 2025, i.e. the loan is contemporaneous with the closing. Whether the loan funded the purchase is still unverified; Cantor declined to give its size or use. Warren/Wyden (29 Apr 2026, answers requested by 13 May) and Blumenthal (8 Oct 2026) sought records, and no public answers were found.

sub_claims.statement: The administration passed stablecoin legislation that benefited Tether/Cantor.
sub_claims.finding: The GENIUS Act became law in July 2025. Tether launched the GENIUS-compliant USAT on 27 Jan 2026 (issuer Anchorage Digital, custodian Cantor, CEO Bo Hines, former White House crypto council director). Critics cite foreign-issuer loopholes. No evidence was found that Lutnick shaped the Act, and Commerce has no stablecoin regulatory role.

sub_claims.statement: Commerce controls AI-chip export licences, creating a Tether-linked conflict.
sub_claims.finding: Commerce (BIS) does license chip exports, including under the UAE deal. No reporting ties Tether or Cantor to any chip-licence decision. Audit addition: Cantor's 13F showed ~$1.19B of Nvidia exposure in Q3 2024 (including large put and call option positions), and a much smaller common position (~1.78M shares, ~$310M, per aggregator data) in Q1 2026; Accountable.US argued in 2025 that this creates a conflict with Commerce's chip oversight (advocacy framing). Axios (11 Nov 2026) reported Lutnick resisted curbs on Megaspeed, a Singapore Nvidia customer accused of diverting chips to China. No reporting links Cantor's holdings or Tether to that decision, so the conflict remains inference.

sub_claims.statement: Cantor launched crypto/bitcoin SPACs, including Twenty One Capital with Tether and SoftBank.
sub_claims.finding: Announced 23 Apr 2025 as a ~$3.6B deal: Tether ~$1.6B in BTC, Bitfinex ~$600M, SoftBank ~$900M. Merged with Cantor Equity Partners (chair/CEO Brandon Lutnick). Listed on the NYSE as XXI on 9 Dec 2025 with >43,500 BTC and $585M of financing.

corrections: 'Held a stake in Tether': it is a $600M convertible bond convertible into ~5%, not direct equity (Lutnick testimony, Bloomberg).
Congress passed the GENIUS Act and Trump signed it. Commerce has no stablecoin regulatory role (Treasury/OCC).
The ~$10B current value of the stake is Sen. Blumenthal's estimate, not a disclosed figure.

Divestiture timing: May 2025 was the announcement and the effective date for BGC/Newmark pieces; the sale of the Cantor interest closed later, on 6 Oct 2025 per his 278-T, the day before the 7 Oct 2025 Tether credit filing (timing only; the loan's purpose is not documented).

2026-11-17 (holdings audit, C104/C105): Claimed: minority stakes went to '26North and Glenn August'; closing 'October 2025'. The record shows: the White House waiver of 8 Jul 2025 names the buyers as 26North, Oak Hill Advisors and Cantor Fitzgerald, L.P. (Glenn August founded Oak Hill); all sale agreements were signed on 16 May 2025 and the Cantor sale closed on 6 Oct 2025 (278-T signed 5 Nov 2025). The 6 Oct sales also include CF Group Management, Inc., his BGC Class B shares and retirement-account shares.

2026-11-17 (holdings audit, C104/C105): Commerce's statement that he 'fully complied' with recusal requirements should be read with the primary record: a limited interim 18 U.S.C. 208(b)(1) waiver (White House Counsel, 8 Jul 2025) let him take part in particular matters of general applicability affecting Cantor, BGC and Newmark until the 6 Oct 2025 closing. It excluded specific-party matters involving the firms and meetings with their representatives. Before 8 Jul he was under the ethics agreement's interim recusal.
denials_and_context: Tether (2024): the relationship is purely professional, about managing reserves, with no regulatory influence from Lutnick's role.

Commerce: Lutnick fully complied with his ethics agreement, including divestiture and recusal requirements. Context: from 8 Jul to 6 Oct 2025 a limited White House waiver under 18 U.S.C. 208(b)(1) authorised his participation in broad policy matters affecting Cantor, BGC and Newmark (not specific-party matters or meetings with the firms).
Cantor: the trusts' purchase was 'funded through multiple sources... at market rates and market prices'. It declined to give the loan's size or use.
Lutnick backed stablecoin audits and 100% Treasury backing at his hearing and denied owning Tether.
The congressional letters come from Democrats in the minority without subpoena power. None alleges a specific crime.

Research limits: the original pages at theblock.co, decrypt.co, bloomberglaw, banking.senate.gov and hsgac.senate.gov were not read directly, so findings rest on search summaries that agree across outlets. Tether's valuation and Cantor's Nvidia holdings were checked in the audit pass; Cantor's other SPACs were not.
